description: IDTA 02008 Time Series Data 1.1: semanticIds (Segment vs Segments), mandatory elements per segment kind, Record structure, timestamp concept descriptions, normative status.

items.question: What is the submodel semanticId of IDTA 02008 Time Series Data v1.1?

citation.section: 2.3, Table 2 Specification of Submodel Template TimeSeries

items.question: Can we name the Time Series submodel 'SensorHistory' instead of TimeSeries?
items.expected_answer: No. The submodel idShort shall always be TimeSeries.

citation.quote: TimeSeries Note: the above idShort shall always be as stated. Class: Submodel

items.question: What semanticId does RecordCount inside a segment have, and which valueType?

citation.section: 2.3, Table 6 Specification of SMC InternalSegment, row RecordCount

items.question: What semanticId identifies an InternalSegment SMC?
items.expected_answer: https://admin-shell.io/idta/TimeSeries/Segments/InternalSegment/1/1 (plural 'Segments' for segment types, unlike the singular 'Segment' of segment fields).

citation.section: 2.3, Table 5 Specification of SMC Segments, row InternalSegment{00}

items.question: Which elements of a LinkedSegment are mandatory?
items.expected_answer: Endpoint (TimeSeries/Endpoint/1/1) and Query (TimeSeries/Query/1/1), each cardinality 1; all other segment fields are 0..1.

citation.quote: server through which time series can be requested n/a 1 [Property] Query [IRI] https://admin-shell.io/idta/TimeSeries/Query/1/1

items.question: In an InternalSegment, which SMC holds the data rows, with what cardinality and collection flags?
items.expected_answer: Records (TimeSeries/Records/1/1), cardinality 1, ordered = true, allowDuplicates = false; it holds Record SMCs (0..n).

items.question: Is a Metadata SMC with only Name and Description complete?
items.expected_answer: No. Metadata also needs the Record SMC (TimeSeries/Record/1/1, cardinality 1) describing the schema (timestamps and variables); Name is mandatory, Description 0..1.

citation.section: 2.3, Table 3 Specification of SMC Metadata, row Record
citation.quote: variable values referenced to the ID ordered = true allowDuplicated = true n/a 1

items.question: Can a single time series record carry more than one timestamp (e.g. sensor time and server time)?
items.expected_answer: Yes. Time{00} has cardinality 1..n in the Record, with semanticIds such as UtcTime, TaiTime, RelativePointInTime or RelativeTimeDuration.

citation.section: 2.3, Table 4 Specification of SMC Record, row Time{00}

items.question: Which semanticId should a 'Temperature' variable in the Record use according to IDTA 02008?
items.expected_answer: The spec does not define semantic IDs for time series variables; choose a suitable one for the measured quantity (e.g. from ECLASS/IEC CDD).

citation.quote: This specification does not define semantic IDs of time series variables.

items.question: IDTA 02008 spells the relative time-point timestamp both RelativePointInTime and RelativeTimePoint. Which IRI does the official 1.1 template use?
items.expected_answer: https://admin-shell.io/idta/TimeSeries/RelativePointInTime/1/1 - the template's concept description has idShort RelativeTimePoint but id .../RelativePointInTime/1/1 (the Table 10 IRI .../RelativeTimePoint/1/1 is the outlier).

citation.document: IDTA 02008 Time Series Data - official template JSON

items.notes: PDF Table 4 (txt page 16) uses RelativePointInTime; Table 10 (page 29) prints RelativeTimePoint.

items.question: Which IEC CDD IRDI may be used instead of the admin-shell.io IRI for a UTC timestamp?

citation.section: 2.4, Table 10 Example Timestamp definitions, row UtcTime

items.question: Which values may a segment's State property take?
How is a segment's Duration expressed with the standard Duration semanticId?
items.expected_answer: As an ISO 8601 duration string in the format P[n]Y[n]M[n]DT[n]H[n]M[n]S (e.g. P3DT4H59M); a long in seconds only with another semanticId.

citation.quote: Period covered by the segment, represented according to ISO 8601 by the format P[n]Y[n]M[n]DT[n]H[n]M[n]S

items.question: Are the ReadSegments/ReadRecords operations part of the normative Time Series 1.1 template?
items.expected_answer: No. The operations are in section 2.6 'Outlook on Time Series Operations', which is not normative yet.

citation.quote: 2.6 Outlook on Time Series Operations - not normative yet
